result:
Lint passed with no error message this time (no blocking hook feedback). The manifest is complete.

## Summary

`/out/manifest.json` decomposes ripgrep into **12 Logical Units**, largely following the repo's existing Cargo workspace crate boundaries (which already encode real architectural seams — each crate is separately published with a narrow public API) plus a split of the `crates/core` binary into "what can be asked" (`cli-flags`) vs. "what actually runs" (`app-orchestration`):

- **glob-matching**, **matcher-contract** — pure domain contracts, no effects
- **ignore-and-walk**, **regex-engine**, **pcre2-engine**, **cli-support**, **grep-facade** — infra (filesystem/subprocess/FFI adapters, or pure glue)
- **line-searcher**, **result-printer**, **index-engine**, **cli-flags**, **app-orchestration** — domain logic

12 scouts ran in parallel to derive each contract from actual code (grepped entrypoint call sites, not guesses). During reconciliation I: dropped two `#[cfg(test)]`-only files the searcher scout correctly flagged as non-runtime; added 6 `include_str!`-embedded template files the cli-flags scout caught; rewrote every `depends_on` edge to route through the `grep-facade` re-export where that's how the code actually imports it (not directly to the underlying crate); and normalized every effect to the schema's enum. One real architectural finding is recorded in `violations_observed`: `cli-flags` and `app-orchestration` are mutually coupled (each calls declared entrypoints of the other) rather than cleanly layered, since both came from the same original `crates/core` binary.

The lint hook flagged one gap (undeclared `clock` effect in `app-orchestration` from `Instant::now()` in `main.rs`), which I fixed; the rewrite produced no further errors.
